acceptance.given: A TC-D1 scope or implementation proposal is evaluated against the retained current Skill-input v2 contract.

oracle.expected: The scope-boundary check rejects a proposal that redesigns Skill-input v1/current-pointer semantics while the existing Skill-input v2 behavior remains retained.
forbidden: Acceptance of a v1/current-pointer semantic redesign as TC-D1 work.
Replacement of current Skill-input v2 behavior with a legacy semantic redesign.
oracle.observable: The boundary-validation result identifies the proposed v1/current-pointer redesign as out of TC-D1 scope and records that Skill-input v2 behavior is retained.

acceptance.then: The evaluated proposal is rejected without changing the current Skill-input v2 behavior.
acceptance.when: The Toolchain scope-boundary validation is executed.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the existing scope-boundary negative validator against a proposal fixture that introduces only a Skill-input v1/current-pointer semantic redesign; require its deterministic scope rejection.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Add Toolchain scope validation that rejects any TC-D1 proposal redesigning Skill-input v1/current-pointer semantics while preserving the current Skill-input v2 behavior.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: The change is limited to a TC-D1 scope rejection. It does not alter the Skill-input v2 selection, content, current-pointer, or retention semantics governed outside this repair.

slice_hint.state_transition: A proposal containing a v1/current-pointer semantic redesign transitions from pending scope evaluation to rejected; proposals retaining current Skill-input v2 behavior remain within the preserved boundary.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Pass only when the scope check rejects the legacy semantic redesign and confirms that current Skill-input v2 behavior has not been replaced.

acceptance.given: A Toolchain verdict is pending evaluation with its source identity and execution record available for inspection.

oracle.expected: The verdict is traceable to current source identity and real execution evidence, with no assistant prose serving as authoritative evidence.
forbidden: Assistant prose is used as the sole or authoritative basis for a verdict.
A verdict is accepted without source or execution evidence.
oracle.observable: The validation inspects the verdict artifact and its referenced current source identity and execution evidence during acceptance evaluation.

acceptance.then: The verdict is evidence-based and independent of assistant prose.
acceptance.when: The Toolchain acceptance selector evaluates whether a verdict may be accepted.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Evaluate a verdict lacking current source identity or real execution evidence and require acceptance validation to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require the Toolchain verdict artifact to bind current source identity and real execution evidence, excluding assistant prose as an evidentiary authority.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted state or schema change; revert removes only the Toolchain verdict-evidence enforcement.

slice_hint.state_transition: unevaluated verdict -> verdict accepted only with inspectable source and execution evidence
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Acceptance evaluation can inspect current source identity and real execution evidence for the verdict and rejects prose-only or evidence-free verdicts.

acceptance.given: A Toolchain aggregate execution is running under its bounded execution controls.

oracle.expected: The aggregate reaches a deterministically identified terminal state; exhaustion of its execution budget is unsuccessful.
forbidden: The aggregate ends in an indeterminate or nondeterministic terminal state.
oracle.observable: The aggregate execution result exposes one deterministic terminal state after the bounded execution ends.

acceptance.then: The aggregate is in a deterministic terminal state.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute a bounded aggregate path that would otherwise end without a deterministic terminal verdict and require a red unsuccessful outcome.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Make each bounded Toolchain aggregate execution emit a deterministic terminal state and classify budget exhaustion as unsuccessful.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted state or schema change; revert restores prior Toolchain aggregate terminal-state handling.

slice_hint.state_transition: aggregate executing -> deterministic successful or unsuccessful terminal state
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Every completed aggregate exposes a deterministic terminal state, and budget exhaustion is unsuccessful.

acceptance.given: A Consumer success-path evaluation is executed against the repository-owned replay implementation with its required Consumer route set and route-invocation evidence available.

oracle.expected: The terminal success result is emitted only when every required Consumer route check is actually reachable and executed on that success path, with attributable invocation evidence for each route.
forbidden: A required Consumer route check is unreachable on a success path.
A successful result is accepted when a required Consumer route check was bypassed.
oracle.observable: The replay result and execution evidence enumerate every required Consumer route check, show an invocation for each on the success path, and reject any missing, unreachable, or bypassed route.

acceptance.then: The success-path evaluation must confirm complete reachability and execution of all required Consumer route checks before returning success.
acceptance.when: A Consumer success path is evaluated.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the success-path route evaluation with one required Consumer route made unreachable or omitted; the evaluator must fail closed and must not produce a successful result.

affected_subjects: Required Consumer routes on Consumer success paths
slice_hint.behavior_change: The replay success-path evaluation verifies and records execution of every required Consumer route check; any unreachable, omitted, or bypassed check prevents success.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing replay result categories and Consumer route interfaces; only strengthen success-path closure so missing route execution fails closed.

slice_hint.state_transition: Consumer success-path evaluation transitions to success only after all required route checks reach and complete their real invocation; otherwise it transitions to an unsuccessful terminal result.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Success is terminally valid iff every required Consumer route check has a reachable, executed invocation with attributable evidence; any missing or bypassed route yields failure.
